purpose: Test two independent backend renewals after access-token expiry, using the refresh credential from the user’s existing My Vodafone web session.
approval: User explicitly approved this two-cycle local experiment, including encrypted credential transfer, retirement of its browser cache entry and retention of the latest encrypted replacement. No requests beyond the two-cycle budget are authorized.

form.refresh_token: <approved session credential; never included in evidence>

sequence: Require one My Vodafone tab and a fresh browser access token
Stage the refresh credential encrypted with the existing local vault key
Remove only the matching Auth0 token-cache entry from that browser origin; leave cookies, other storage and account data alone
Navigate the donor tab to the extension’s research status page
After the old access token expires, exchange its refresh credential and verify one account API read
Save the rotated refresh credential encrypted before API verification
After that access token expires, perform one more renewal and account read
Stop automatically after the second exchange or the first failure; retain the latest credential encrypted for review
constraints: No client registration or new OAuth authorization request
No browser cookies, passwords or client secret sent by the backend
No automatic retries or restart recovery
No simultaneous browser/backend use of the same refresh-token family
No credential values in logs, API responses or public evidence
The user may need to sign in to My Vodafone again afterward
expectedDuration: About ten minutes; the backend waits for natural access-token expiry. Edge can be used normally once the donor tab has handed off.
retention: The research vault keeps the current refresh credential encrypted locally for approved follow-up. It does not start indefinite renewal.

implementation.userAction: Run approved renewal test in the VodaLens popup

execution.latestRefreshCredential: Retained encrypted in the ignored local research vault
